results.title: Approaching asymptotes
results.description: This algebra-free resource is designed to provoke discussion and help build up students’ sense of what asymptotes are.  This extends ideas beyond the classic example of $y=\tfrac{1}{x}$, which is used as a warm-up.

results.title: Function squares

results.title: How many roots does this equation have?

results.title: Mapping a function
results.description: Students are introduced to using mapping diagrams as a way to visualise a function; this is developed in later resources to visualise derivatives and then to understand the chain rule.

results.title: Odd or even or...
results.description: In this activity students are asked to decide whether functions are odd or even or have some other kind of symmetry. As well as working with the graphs and equations of functions, there are opportunities to think about the effects of graph transformations.

results.title: Picture the process I
results.description: Students are asked to relate real life situations to their algebraic models via graphical representations. This offers lots of opportunities for discussion as well as reflection on working with different representations.

results.title: Piece it together
results.description: Students are asked to describe four piecewise graphs for others to sketch. This may encourage informal discussion about the domains of different sections and help students to develop ideas of how we might write equations of piecewise functions. To take the task further, a set of equations that match to some of the graphs is provided.

results.title: That's odd ... or even
results.description: A formal introduction to odd and even functions: students are asked to evaluate functions at 1, −1, 2, −2, and so on, and then asked to sketch the functions. Students may start to notice common features when evaluating the functions. The relationship between these features and the formal definitions of odd and even functions can then be discussed.

results.title: Two-way functions
results.description: This resource gives students an opportunity to explore their understanding of roots and asymptotes of functions, both by identifying properties that functions have in common and also by seeking functions that have particular properties. For detailed notes on this resource, please see [Two-way functions - teacher support](/thinking-about-functions/two-way-functions-teacher-support).

Then they are given several graphs and asked to decide which gives the best representation of a particular function that they are unlikely to have met before.

results.title: Make it equal
results.description: Different particles are in equilibrium, each with three forces acting upon them. Students are given two of the forces and encouraged to use different approaches in order to find the third force.

results.title: Make it stop!
results.description: Given a particle moving under a system of forces, students are asked to add a further force to bring the particle to rest in a specified time. This offers opportunities to combine various ideas about vectors with kinematics and Newton's laws of motion.

results.title: One windy day
results.description:
In this task, students are asked to model a projectile situation with the added effect of an acceleration due to the wind.
This leads to some work with parametric equations of curves.
